A per-session match-count rollup shows which sessions are worth drilling into. There is no pagination — if the top results miss, refine the query instead of paging.

Scope:
  omitted or "current": only the current session
  "all": every persisted session
  "project:<name>": sessions whose project directory ends with <name> (case-insensitive; name is matched against the final path component)
  a specific session: pass session_id directly

Drill into a hit with session_fetch using its entry id.

Examples:
  session_search({"query": "rowid mapping"})
  session_search({"query": "fts5 snippet", "scope": "all", "fields": ["assistant", "tool_result"]})
  session_search({"query": "compactor", "scope": "project:session-search"})

dump_to_disk.description: Optional file path to write this tool's full result to; the in-context response becomes a short pointer + preview.

fields.description: Entry roles to search. Defaults to ['assistant', 'user']. 'actor' and 'thinking' are never indexed.

limit.description: Maximum number of hits to return (1-50). Defaults to 20.

query.description: FTS5 MATCH expression, e.g. 'auth flow', '"retry with backoff"', 'migrat*', 'tool_result NEAR(timeout config)'.

scope.description: Where to search: omit for the current session, 'all' for every persisted session, or 'project:<name>' for sessions in that project (name matched against the last path component, case-insensitive).

session_id.description: Search exactly one session by id (overrides scope).

since.description: Only entries on or after this ISO date/datetime (e.g. '2026-09-01' or '2026-09-01T12:00:00Z').

until.description: Only entries on or before this ISO date/datetime.

prompt_guidelines: Prefer session_search over re-reading old sessions entry by entry; it finds content in sessions that were never loaded.
Queries are FTS5 MATCH expressions — if the syntax is wrong the SQLite error is returned verbatim; fix and retry.

tool_definitions.name: skill
tool_definitions.description: Load a specific agent skill's content into the conversation context. The skill content is returned in this tool result and pinned in the conversation history for the rest of the conversation. Use this tool when the current task matches a skill's description from the available skills list. Do not call this tool if the skill is already loaded (marked loaded='true' in the available skills list).

dump_to_disk.description: Optional file path to write this tool's full result to; the in-context response becomes a short pointer + preview.

name.description: The name of the skill to load (from the available skills list)

tool_definitions.name: spawn_subagent
tool_definitions.description:
Delegate a self-contained task to a fresh subagent session.

Each call creates one subagent. To use multiple subagents, make multiple spawn_subagent
calls in the same assistant turn. Subagents inherit the model, cwd, tools,
skills, and MCP servers, but not the parent conversation history or the parent
task list — a subagent starts with an empty task list and receives its entire
assignment in the prompt. Only the subagent's final message is returned; its
intermediate tool calls and output remain in its own context.

WHEN TO USE:
 - open-ended exploration or research
 - multi-step work whose intermediate output you do not need
 - broad reviews, comparisons, investigations, or implementation work that contains multiple independent concerns
 - work that can be divided into separate, bounded workstreams

WHEN NOT TO USE: the work can run in the background while you continue (a bot
reports back as a message and never blocks you), or the same worker should
handle several dispatches over time — use load_bot + tell_session instead.

**AVOID SPAWNING INDIVIDUAL SUBAGENTS. PREFER SPAWNING 2+ SUBAGENTS WITH EXPLICIT BOUNDED TASKS**

PARALLEL DELEGATION DEFAULT:

For requests containing two or more independent workstreams, the default is
to delegate each workstream to a separate subagent and launch the first wave
concurrently.

Before making the first spawn_subagent call:
 1. Identify the relevant workstreams.
 2. Separate independent work from dependent work.
 3. For each independent workstream, write a distinct, self-contained brief.
 4. Emit all first-wave spawn_subagent calls in the same assistant turn.

Do not default to one subagent merely because this tool creates one subagent
per call. Multiple calls are the mechanism for fan-out.

A single call is appropriate when the work is genuinely indivisible, very
small, strictly sequential, or when delegation would cost more than doing the
work directly.

USE WAVES FOR DEPENDENT WORK:

For dependent tasks, launch only the independent portion of the current wave
concurrently. After collecting those results, determine the next wave from
their outputs.

The parent agent remains responsible for:
 - assigning clear boundaries to each workstream
 - collecting and comparing results
 - identifying duplicate or conflicting findings
 - resolving conflicts and integrating changes
 - performing final verification

Do not parallelize work that:
 - depends directly on another task's result
 - would duplicate substantially the same investigation
 - is too small to benefit from delegation
 - requires multiple agents to modify the same files concurrently

For concurrent code changes, assign disjoint files or scopes. Prefer parallel
read-only investigation when ownership is unclear; let the parent integrate
the changes.

EXAMPLES:
 - "Find relevant implementation files" + "Find relevant tests" -> two concurrent spawn_subagent calls.
 - "Review correctness" + "Review security" + "Review test coverage" -> three concurrent spawn_subagent calls.
 - "Investigate possible causes A and B" -> two concurrent calls, followed by parent synthesis.
 - "Implement A, then use A's result to implement B" -> sequential waves.
 - "Make changes to files A, B, C" -> three concurrent spawn_subagent calls.

PROMPT REQUIREMENTS:
 - The prompt must be self-contained: the subagent cannot see this conversation
   or the user's original intent.
 - State the goal, relevant context, constraints, scope, and expected result.
 - Avoid giving multiple overlapping workstreams to the same subagent.

TIMEOUT: unlimited by default. Pass max_duration_secs to bound the
subagent; on expiry the subagent is cancelled and a failure is returned.

description.description: A 3-5 word summary of the task, shown as the subagent session's title in the sidebar.

dump_to_disk.description: Optional file path to write this tool's full result to; the in-context response becomes a short pointer + preview.

model.description: Optional model override for the subagent. The value must name an expanded provider/model id (e.g. "openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4") or a configured alias name (e.g. "fast"); anything else fails the call before any subagent is created. Defaults to this session's model. Do not provide empty strings or use 'inherit' as the model. Use this field only when the user explicitly instructs a model for the subagent — you almost never need to do this.

prompt.description: Self-contained brief for the subagent. It sees nothing else — no conversation history, no user intent.

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Delegate one self-contained workstream to a fresh subagent. For multiple independent workstreams, make multiple spawn_subagent calls in the same assistant turn.
prompt_guidelines: Before delegating, identify independent workstreams and their dependencies. If two or more workstreams can proceed without waiting for each other, launch them concurrently as separate spawn_subagent calls in the same assistant turn.

Treat fan-out as the default for multi-part work. Do not stop after one subagent when the request contains additional independent concerns. Use one subagent only when the work is tiny, indivisible, strictly sequential, or not worth coordinating.
Start with a small bounded fan-out, typically 2–4 subagents, and increase it only when the workstreams are substantial, clearly independent, and non-conflicting.
For dependent work, use waves: launch the independent tasks in the current wave, collect and synthesize their results, then launch the next wave.
Give each subagent a distinct scope. Avoid overlapping prompts, and do not ask multiple agents to edit the same files concurrently. Prefer read-only investigation when file ownership is unclear.
Write every subagent prompt as a complete brief: goal, context, constraints, relevant paths or symbols, whether to research or make changes, and the expected output.

A subagent starts with an empty task list; it does not see yours. Put the entire assignment in the prompt — the subagent must not be expected to read context from your task list, and its todo mutations never propagate back to you.

The model argument is only for when the user explicitly instructs a model for a subagent — you almost never need it. Its value must be an expanded provider/model id or a configured alias name; an unknown name fails the call without spawning anything.

tool_definitions.name: tell_session
tool_definitions.description: Send a message to another session by its session id. An idle bot starts a run seeded from its template plus your message; a busy bot receives it when its current turn finishes; any other session receives it as a new user turn. With mode "interrupt" on a busy target, the message lands as a steering fragment at its next prompt-assembly boundary instead of queueing.

dump_to_disk.description: Optional file path to write this tool's full result to; the in-context response becomes a short pointer + preview.

message.description: The message text the target session receives. Markdown format is supported.

mode.description: How the message is delivered to a busy target: "queue" (the default) waits for its current turn to finish; "interrupt" lands it as a steering fragment at the target's next prompt-assembly boundary, without cancelling in-flight work. An interrupt to an idle target delivers ordinarily.

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Deliver a message to a named session: `tell_session` with the target session id and the text. Pass mode "interrupt" to steer a busy session's current turn; the default mode queues.
prompt_guidelines: Use `tell_session` to hand work to a specific session — a stage bot in a workflow run, or any session whose id you know. Never guess an id; use one you were given or can read.

tool_definitions.name: todo_get_list
tool_definitions.description: Get the full todo list with all phases and tasks. Returns the current state of the todo list, plus the next task to work on.

dump_to_disk.description: Optional file path to write this tool's full result to; the in-context response becomes a short pointer + preview.

tool_definitions.name: todo_set_list
tool_definitions.description: Replace the entire task list with a new one. Accepts an ordered list of phases, each containing an ordered list of tasks. The list you send IS the list - anything omitted is deleted, and task statuses are declared inline, not remembered. Each task is an object with 'description' and 'status' (pending, completed, or cancelled). Pass an empty phases array to clear the task list entirely. Use this when you have a complete plan ready to materialize; use todo_set_phase for day-to-day updates.

dump_to_disk.description: Optional file path to write this tool's full result to; the in-context response becomes a short pointer + preview.

phases.description: Ordered list of phases. Each phase has a description and an optional list of tasks. An empty array clears the task list.

tasks.description: Ordered list of tasks for this phase. An empty or omitted list is valid.

status.description: Declared status of this task. 'pending' if the work has not been done yet.

prompt_guidelines: Provide the full plan - all phases and tasks - in a single call. Existing phases and tasks are replaced entirely.
Each phase must have a description. Tasks within a phase are optional.
Read the current list first (todo_get_list) and include everything you want to keep - anything omitted is deleted.
Send every task as an object with both fields: {"description": "...", "status": "pending"} (statuses: pending, completed, cancelled).
'postponed' is not a valid status - move the task to a later phase or cancel it instead.
Pass an empty phases array ({"phases": []}) to clear the task list entirely.

tool_definitions.name: todo_set_phase
tool_definitions.description: Write one entire phase of the task list, matched by its description. If a phase with this description exists, it is replaced (first match wins); otherwise the phase is appended to the end of the list. Tasks declare their status inline: each task is an object with 'description' and 'status' (pending, completed, or cancelled). Use this for day-to-day updates - write the entire phase including unchanged tasks; use todo_set_list to restructure the whole list.

description.description: Description of the phase to write. Matched exactly against existing phase descriptions; appended as a new phase when nothing matches.

dump_to_disk.description: Optional file path to write this tool's full result to; the in-context response becomes a short pointer + preview.

tasks.description: The complete ordered task list for this phase. An empty or omitted list is valid.

status.description: Declared status of this task. 'pending' if the work has not been done yet.

prompt_guidelines: Write the ENTIRE phase - every task you want it to contain, including unchanged ones. Tasks left out of the payload are removed from the phase.
Phase matching is exact (case-sensitive) on the trimmed description. If no phase matches, a new phase is appended and the result says so - check for typos when that wasn't intended.
Record progress by resending the phase with statuses flipped: {"description": "...", "status": "completed"}. Every task needs both a 'description' and a 'status' (pending, completed, cancelled).
'postponed' is not a valid status - move the task to a later phase or cancel it instead.
To finish a whole phase and move on, flip all its tasks to completed (or cancelled) in one call.

tool_definitions.name: write
tool_definitions.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting the existing file 
            if one exists at the provided path. Parent directories are created automatically.


            Prefer editing existing files; never create new files unless required, and never 
            create documentation files (*.md, README) unless the user explicitly asks.

content.description: The content to write to the file

dump_to_disk.description: Optional file path to write this tool's full result to; the in-context response becomes a short pointer + preview.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write

prompt_guidelines: Only use `write` for new files or complete rewrites — use `edit` for changes.
